_comment: JSON has no comment syntax, so this change history lives in a field instead. Unity's JsonUtility ignores fields that QuizData does not declare, so this is read by people only and can be deleted with no effect on the game.
_changeHistory: 2026-09-16 - Claude Code - Added 32 credentialed technician level questions after the original 10, covering dosage and fluid rate math, anesthesia monitoring and reversal agents, breathing circuits and oxygen supply, hematology and urinalysis interpretation, dentistry, radiographic exposure factors, CPR per RECOVER, toxicology and transfusion medicine. The original 10 questions were not modified.
2026-09-16 - Claude Code - Correct answers in the added questions are spread across all four positions, so the bank cannot be gamed by always guessing A or B.

questions.question: A Fecal Flotation tests for all the following parasites, EXCEPT:
What is a purple top tube used for?

answers.B: Collecting whole blood to spin down for plasma.
answers.D: It's a sterile tube that can be used for any type of sample.

questions.question: What is the Distemper vaccine for?

answers.A: The distemper vaccine makes dogs behave better, by controlling their temper.
answers.C: To prevent certain species of ticks
answers.D: The Distemper vaccine contains a combination of 4 to 5 vaccines that prevent different GI and Upper Respiratory diseases.

questions.question: What is dermataphyte? WHat is the best way to test for it?

answers.A: It is a bacterium thats tested for by checking a skin cytology.
answers.B: It is a fungus thats tested for by taking a sample of the fur and growing that sample on a sterile medium or running a Dermatophyte PCR.
answers.C: It is a protozoa that tested for by checking a fecal floation
answers.D: It is a fungus thats tested for by checking a fecal smear.

questions.question: What is the difference between a LIPOMA and PAPILLOMA?

answers.B: A lipoma is a pimple and a papilloma is a zit.
answers.C: A lipoma is benign fatty mass and a papilloma is benign wart.
answers.D: A lipoma is a cancerous tumour and a papilloma is a benign tumour.

questions.question: Which of the following species can contract Rabies?

answers.A: Only mammalian species can contract Rabies.
answers.B: Eagles, Pythons, Humans, Whales, and Canines.
answers.C: Iguanas, Vipers, Axolotls, Salamanders, and Geckos.

questions.question: What position should a patient be in for a right lateral abdominal radiograph?

answers.B: Laying with their left side down.
answers.D: Laying with their right side down.

questions.question: How do you test for ear mites?

answers.A: Get a skin scrapinhg for a skin cytology.

questions.question: What position should a patient be in for a OFA radiograph of the hips?
Which of the following is NOT a way to test for fleas?

answers.A: Check a fecal smear under the microscope.
answers.B: Check for flea dirt using a black light.
answers.C: Use a flea comb to remove fleas from the fur.
answers.D: Comb out a small amount of fur and use peroxide to check for flea dirt.

questions.question: A 22 lb dog is prescribed cefazolin at 22 mg/kg. What is the total dose?
A patient needs 75 mg of a drug that is supplied at 50 mg/mL. What volume do you draw up?
A 20 kg dog is to receive maintenance fluids at 60 mL/kg/day. What is the hourly rate?
You are running fluids at 50 mL/hr on a 15 drop/mL administration set. What is the drip rate?
What is the shock dose of isotonic crystalloids for a dog, and how is it given?

answers.B: 10 to 15 mL/kg as a slow drip over an hour.
answers.C: 80 to 90 mL/kg, given in smaller boluses of 1/4 to 1/3 of the dose with reassessment between each.

questions.question: Which of these anesthetic drugs provides NO analgesia?
Which drug reverses dexmedetomidine?
Naloxone is the reversal agent for which drug class?
Your patient is on 3% isoflurane and becomes bradycardic and hypotensive. What is your first action?

answers.A: Turn the vaporizer up to deepen the plane.
answers.C: Turn the vaporizer down and alert the veterinarian.

questions.question: What does capnography measure, and what is a normal range under anesthesia?

answers.B: End tidal carbon dioxide, 35 to 45 mmHg
answers.C: Respiratory rate, 8 to 20 breaths per minute

questions.question: Your anesthetized patient's SpO2 reads 88%. What does that tell you?

answers.A: The patient is hypoxemic and needs intervention now.
answers.C: This is normal and needs no action.

questions.question: What is the minimum acceptable mean arterial pressure (MAP) for an anesthetized patient?
A non-rebreathing circuit is generally chosen for patients under what body weight?

answers.D: Body weight does not matter when choosing a circuit.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the pop-off (adjustable pressure limiting) valve?

answers.A: It vents excess gas from the breathing circuit so pressure cannot build up.
answers.B: It measures the patient's tidal volume.
answers.C: It delivers anesthetic gas to the patient.
answers.D: It absorbs carbon dioxide from exhaled gas.

questions.question: The granules in the CO2 absorbent canister have changed color and feel hard and crumbly. What does that mean?

answers.B: The absorbent is exhausted, can no longer remove CO2, and must be replaced.
answers.C: The vaporizer needs to be refilled.

questions.question: An E cylinder of oxygen reads 500 psi. About how many liters are left?
What is in a green top tube and what does it give you?

answers.A: A clot activator, which gives serum.
answers.B: EDTA, which gives whole blood for a CBC.
answers.C: Lithium heparin, which gives plasma for chemistry.
answers.D: Sodium citrate, which gives plasma for coagulation testing.

questions.question: What is a blue top (sodium citrate) tube used for?

answers.D: Coagulation testing such as PT and aPTT.

questions.question: What happens to your results if an EDTA tube is significantly underfilled?

answers.A: The excess anticoagulant shrinks the red cells, falsely lowering the PCV and red cell indices.
answers.B: The total protein is falsely increased.
answers.C: Nothing, fill volume does not matter in a CBC tube.
answers.D: The sample will read as hemolyzed every time.

questions.question: Which part of a blood smear do you use to perform the differential and evaluate cell morphology?

answers.B: The monolayer, just behind the feathered edge
answers.C: The thick body of the smear
answers.D: Any area, as long as the stain looks good

questions.question: After spinning a microhematocrit tube, what is the buffy coat made of?
What does a refractometer measure in the lab?

answers.D: Urine specific gravity and total solids/protein.

questions.question: A dehydrated, azotemic cat has a urine specific gravity of 1.010. What does that indicate?

answers.B: Isosthenuria, meaning the kidneys are not concentrating urine, which is consistent with renal disease.
answers.C: The sample was contaminated and should be ignored.

questions.question: Which parasite is best detected with a zinc sulfate flotation rather than a standard sugar or salt solution?
You see 'coffin lid' shaped crystals in a urine sediment. What are they?
How should an ultrasonic scaler tip be used during a dental prophylaxis?

answers.A: Held against one tooth surface for 30 seconds or more to be thorough.
answers.B: Kept moving, using the side of the tip with water flowing, for only a few seconds per tooth.
answers.C: Pressed point first into the gingival sulcus.
answers.D: Used dry so you can see the calculus better.

questions.question: What is a normal periodontal probing depth in a dog?

answers.C: Probing depth has no clinical meaning.

questions.question: Using the modified Triadan system, which tooth is 104?
On a radiograph, what does increasing the kVp primarily change?

answers.A: The energy and penetrating power of the beam, which changes the scale of contrast.
answers.B: Nothing, kVp only matters on digital systems.
answers.C: Only the number of x-ray photons produced.

questions.question: Per RECOVER guidelines, what is the correct chest compression rate and depth for CPR in a dog?

answers.A: 150 per minute, as deep as you can go.
answers.B: 100 to 120 per minute, compressing 1/3 to 1/2 of the chest width.
answers.D: 60 to 80 per minute, compressing 1/4 of the chest.

questions.question: A cat is presented after chewing on an Easter lily. What is the primary concern?

answers.C: Nothing, lilies are only toxic to dogs

questions.question: Why must cats be blood typed before their FIRST transfusion, even though dogs usually are not?

answers.A: Typing is done to determine the volume of blood to give.
answers.B: Cats only have one blood type, so typing is a formality.
answers.C: Cats have naturally occurring alloantibodies, so a type mismatch can cause a fatal reaction on the first transfusion.
answers.D: Cats cannot receive transfusions at all.
